# Results — Study 804 (Realized-Kurtosis Premium)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Amaya,
Christoffersen, Jacobs & Vasquez (2015): alongside the strong negative realized-**skewness**
relation, the same paper tests realized **kurtosis** and finds it a **weak / ambiguous**
predictor, mostly subsumed by skewness and volatility. We sort on trailing realized kurtosis
and test the specified long-high-kurt / short-low-kurt book. Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the
last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `357fd262912f`
(panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's **trailing-21-day realized kurtosis** of daily simple returns (population 4th standardised central moment `m4 / m2**2`, vectorised via rolling raw moments — **not** `rolling.apply`), known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by the signal; **long the top 30%** (high kurt), **short the bottom 30%** (low kurt), equal-weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled high-vs-low books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. As in the
skewness sibling, the realized-moment premia are documented as **small-and-illiquid-stock**
effects; a 50-mega-cap survivor panel is exactly where they are *least* likely to appear.

## The headline — long-high-kurt / short-low-kurt spread

Daily equal-weight top-30% minus bottom-30% realized-kurtosis spread (n = **4,125** days):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long high-kurt − short low-kurt)** | **+1.78 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **+1.79** |
| one-sample *t* | +1.76 |
| high-kurt book / low-kurt book | +8.76 bps / +6.97 bps (Welch *t* = +0.69) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | +0.43 |

The specified direction has the **right sign** — high-kurt names slightly out-earned low-kurt
ones — but the effect is **not robust**: the Newey-West *t* is **+1.79**, below the desk's |t| ≥ 2
bar, and the pooled book Welch *t* is a limp +0.69. This is exactly the paper's own verdict on
kurtosis: a **weak / ambiguous** signal, not the strong result skewness delivers. **Weak.**

## Placebo — is the (weak) relation a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the trailing-kurt sort but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted**
panel (signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **+1.78 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.004 bps (0.825) |
| position of observed | ≈ **+2.16σ into the right tail** (right-tail p = **0.016**) |

The permutation null centres at zero and the observed spread sits ~2.2σ into the right tail
(p = 0.016) — so the small positive spread is **not a look-ahead artefact of the sort**. But a
permutation test ignores the serial correlation of the overlapping-window signal, which the
Newey-West *t* (+1.79) does not: the honest robust test is the one that *fails* to clear 2. The
spread is real-ish but too weak to stamp green.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,991) | +0.13 bps | **+0.11** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | +3.33 bps | **+2.12** |

The whole (weak) effect lives in the **second half**: the first era is a flat **zero**
(*t* = +0.11), and only 2018–2026 is marginally significant (*t* = +2.12). A signal that is
absent for eight years and barely clears 2 in the other is the definition of **fragile /
weak** — not a stable premium.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +1.78 bps | 2.14 bps | **−0.35 bps** | −0.35 | −0.09 | −0.9%/yr |
| **5 bps** | +1.78 bps | 10.14 bps | **−8.35 bps** | −8.23 | −2.03 | −21.0%/yr |

The +1.78 bps/day gross edge is **smaller than the 2.14 bps/day round-trip friction at a mere
1 bp one-way**, so the book is net-negative before any realistic cost and deeply so at 5 bps.
**Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel with a persistent latent "kurtosis tilt" that inflates each name's
fat-tailedness (via a two-component Gaussian mixture) and (with `edge>0`) lifts its forward
mean. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.35** (sd 0.90), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.010`, seed 804) | **+12.81** (Welch *t* = +15.36) |

The detector recovers a *planted* positive kurt→return relation cleanly and never fires on the
null — so the weak real-tape spread is a faithful measurement, not a machinery artefact.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The realized-kurtosis premium is, as the source paper itself reports, a
  **weak / ambiguous** signal. On 50 liquid US mega-caps the specified long-high-kurt /
  short-low-kurt spread is **+1.78 bps/day** — the *right sign*, but Newey-West *t* = **+1.79**
  (below the |t| ≥ 2 bar), the book Welch *t* is +0.69, and the effect is a flat zero in
  2010–2017 (*t* = +0.11), surfacing only marginally in 2018–2026 (*t* = +2.12). The 20-seed
  synthetic control is clean (fires 0/20 on the null, recovers a planted relation at *t* =
  +12.81), so this is an honest weak measurement, not a bug. Survivorship biases the magnitude.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The +1.78 bps/day gross edge is already smaller than the 2.14
  bps/day round-trip friction at 1 bp one-way (net **−0.35 bps/day**), and collapses to −8.35
  bps/day at 5 bps. No version of the book survives costs.
